title: IQ band lookup falls through to 'Low' for VFS in the gaps between bands (e.g. 84.995)
claim: Bands use vfs_max 84.99/69.99/54.99 against next band vfs_min 85/70/55; any VFS with 3+ decimals in the gap matches no band and the loop fallback is bands[-1] ('Low'). Verified: predict_iq(84.995,0.8) and predict_iq(69.995,0.8) both return classification 'Low'. VFS is rounded to 1 decimal in the pipeline, but the MCP tool tool_predict_iq accepts any float.
impact_on_screened_person: A person scoring just under a band boundary is silently classified in the lowest band, a gross misclassification with no error.
fix: Use half-open intervals (vfs_min <= vfs < next min) with the top band closed, and raise on out-of-range input instead of defaulting to the last band.

title: predict_iq accepts out-of-range VFS and confidence: percentile 354, negative percentile, inverted CI
claim: No validation of vfs (0-100) or confidence (0-1). Verified: predict_iq(150,.8) -> percentile 354; predict_iq(-5,.8) -> percentile -11, class 'Low'; predict_iq(50,5) -> ci_low 119 > ci_high 49. tool_predict_iq exposes this directly over MCP.
impact_on_screened_person: Impossible scores (percentile 354, inverted CI) can be returned and attached to a person's record.
fix: Validate ranges at the tool boundary and in mapper functions; raise ValueError with a clear message; clamp percentile to 1-99.

title: server.py cannot import under the installed mcp 2.x; fastmcp unpinned and the MCP layer is untested
claim: server.py imports mcp.server.fastmcp, but requirements.txt has unpinned fastmcp>=0.4.0 and the venv resolved mcp 2.3.0 where that module no longer exists, so importing server raises ModuleNotFoundError. No test imports server.py, so CI never catches it; the shipped product entry point is unverified.
impact_on_screened_person: The tool cannot be started by consumers, and screening workflows fail or fall back to ad-hoc unaudited paths.
fix: Pin mcp/fastmcp to a tested range, add tests/test_server.py that imports server and calls every tool, and lock dependencies.

title: Dependencies unpinned and no lockfile: scores can change with upstream upgrades
claim: requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt use >= floors only (spacy, sentence-transformers, textstat, lexicalrichness, sklearn, numpy, ruff). Golden scores in tests/fixtures depend on exact library behaviour; a textstat or spaCy upgrade silently shifts a person's IQ estimate. No pyproject, constraints or hashes.
impact_on_screened_person: The same text may yield a different score and classification after a routine install, with no record of why.
fix: Pin exact versions (pip-compile lockfile), run CI against the lock, and record dependency and model versions in every report.

title: Scores carry no model/norm/version provenance for reproducibility or audit
claim: Output JSON has no score_version, norm file hash, spaCy/sentence-transformer model version, or tool version. Norm files (iq_norms.json) have no version field. A stored score cannot be tied to the algorithm that produced it, and changing norms invalidates history invisibly.

evidence.excerpt: absence: no version/hash field in norms file

impact_on_screened_person: A contested decision cannot be reproduced or defended since the producing algorithm version is unknown.
fix: Add scoring_version, norms_sha256 and model identifiers to vfs/iq/report outputs; bump on any weight or norm change.

title: Empty or non-alphabetic input crashes the pipeline with KeyError
claim: analyze_lexical returns {'score':0.0,'error':...} without lexical_density when no alphabetic tokens exist; run_pipeline then indexes lex['lexical_density']. Verified: run_pipeline('12345 6789 !!!') and run_pipeline('') raise KeyError 'lexical_density'. Over MCP the same shape feeds estimate_education_level and the reporter.
impact_on_screened_person: Unusable submissions crash instead of being rejected as insufficient input; an error dict with score 0.0 could be read as a real zero.
fix: Return a typed InsufficientText result (score None) and make downstream tools refuse to score; add a minimum-words gate.

title: A score of 0.0 is emitted on failure, and short text yields a fabricated 50.0 semantic score
claim: Failure paths return numeric scores (lexical 0.0 on error; semantic 50.0 for <2 sentences) that are then blended into VFS with full weight and only a confidence label, so a missing metric becomes a plausible number.
impact_on_screened_person: A person with one long sentence receives a neutral 50 on 25% of their score instead of an explicit 'not measurable'.
fix: Return score None with reason; VFS must renormalise weights or refuse to produce an IQ when a component is unmeasurable.

title: Malformed JSON args raise uncaught JSONDecodeError across MCP tools (incl. segment_boundaries_json)
claim: Every tool calls json.loads on caller strings with no try/except or schema check; tool_analyze_semantic does so for segment_boundaries_json. Verified pattern: bad JSON propagates as a raw exception; wrong shapes (missing 'idx'/'text') raise KeyError.
impact_on_screened_person: Tool failures are opaque; callers may retry with defaults or skip metrics, producing a score on partial data.
fix: Add a _parse_json helper returning structured {error, field} responses and validate shapes with pydantic or jsonschema.

title: MCP tools inconsistent on language and input validation (lang not validated outside preprocess)
claim: Only preprocess_text validates lang. tool_analyze_* accept any lang string; unknown values silently use the English path (syntactic/readability) and tool_detect_language coerces every non-en/id language (e.g. French, Javanese) to 'en' with confidence 0.50 rather than rejecting.

evidence.excerpt: raise ValueError(f"Unsupported language: {lang!r}. Must be 'en' or 'id'.")

impact_on_screened_person: Non-English/Indonesian writers are scored against English norms as if they were English.
fix: Return lang 'unsupported' and refuse scoring; validate lang in every tool via a shared enum.

title: No input size limit: 1M-character text crashes spaCy; large inputs are unbounded in memory/time
claim: preprocess_text passes the whole cleaned text to nlp(). Verified: 1.25M chars raises ValueError E088. No max length on any MCP tool; semantic encodes every sentence at once and the O(n) per-sentence spaCy calls in syntactic are uncapped. Denial-of-service on a shared server.
impact_on_screened_person: Large corpora (multi-file candidates) error out or hang rather than get a bounded, documented treatment.
fix: Enforce MAX_CHARS with a clear error, chunk long texts, batch_size on encode, and test the limit.

title: Per-sentence nlp() calls and quadratic-ish loops in syntactic/semantic hurt long-text performance
claim: syntactic calls nlp(sent_data['text']) once per sentence instead of nlp.pipe; semantic calls cosine_similarity per adjacent pair in a Python loop; Sastrawi StemmerFactory().create_stemmer() is rebuilt on every analyze_lexical call (slow dictionary load).
impact_on_screened_person: Slow turnaround at scale pushes operators toward truncating text, which changes scores.
fix: Use nlp.pipe, cache the stemmer at module level, vectorise adjacent similarities with a row-wise dot product.

title: Model loading is unguarded: duplicate spaCy caches, no thread safety, no friendly error when models are missing
claim: _get_nlp is duplicated in preprocess.py, syntactic.py and semantic.py with separate caches (the same model loaded up to 3 times). spacy.load/SentenceTransformer raise raw OSError/network errors if the model is absent; SentenceTransformer downloads from Hugging Face at first call at request time. No lock around the check-then-set.
impact_on_screened_person: First request hangs or fails; a different pipeline config in each module can make scores differ from preprocessing.
fix: Centralise model loading in one module with a lock, preload at startup, pin model revisions, and fail with an actionable message.

title: Non-determinism not controlled for model inference; only langdetect seeded
claim: DetectorFactory.seed=42 is the only seeding. langdetect/langid disagreement paths and sentence-transformers/numpy have no pinned revision or deterministic flag; golden tests tolerate nothing but depend on one machine's float output. The model name has no revision hash.
impact_on_screened_person: A rerun on another machine may yield a different classification for the same person.
fix: Pin model revision, add cross-platform tolerance bounds in golden tests, and document determinism guarantees.

title: Reporter hardcodes 'N/A (no parser for id)' for any None dependency depth
claim: The report prints 'no parser for id' whenever dependency_depth is None regardless of language, so a future None for EN would be mislabelled; the reason string lives in the reporter rather than the metric result.

evidence.excerpt: f"  Dependency tree depth : {_dep_depth if _dep_depth is not None else 'N/A (no parser for id)'}"

impact_on_screened_person: Misleading explanation for why a metric is missing weakens transparency to the screened person.
fix: Carry a not_measured_reason field from the analyzer and render it.

title: Reporter indexes result dicts directly (KeyError on error/partial results) and 'Generated' date breaks determinism
claim: generate_report subscripts lexical_result['mattr'], semantic_result['argument_coherence'] etc. with no .get; an error-dict from analyze_lexical, or a None coherence from short text, either crashes or prints 'None'. date.today() is embedded, so reports are not byte-reproducible.
impact_on_screened_person: Reports for borderline submissions fail or show 'None' values to the reader.
fix: Render 'not measured' for None/missing metrics and accept an injectable report date.

title: Mental age and CI accept impossible chronological ages and confidence
claim: predict_mental_age accepts any age (verified -5 -> -5.0, 500 -> 500.0); the ratio formula is applied to adults. tool_predict_mental_age maps 0 and negatives to the default 30 silently.

evidence.excerpt: age = chronological_age if chronological_age > 0 else None

impact_on_screened_person: A mistyped or negative age yields nonsense or a silently assumed age 30 feeding an 'age' conclusion.
fix: Validate 3<=age<=120 and error otherwise; never silently substitute.

title: No logging or observability anywhere in the server
claim: No logging import or audit trail in mcp-server. Failed analyses, language-coercion decisions, model loads and exceptions are not recorded; a score cannot be traced to input hash, version and timestamp.

evidence.excerpt: absence: no logging/audit calls in server.py or tools/*.py

impact_on_screened_person: No accountability record exists to investigate or contest an individual's score.
fix: Add structured logging with input hash, versions, lang decision and warnings (no raw text).

title: CI: ruff unpinned (0.17 reports lint errors), spaCy models and sentence-transformer weights not cached, ruff ignores scripts/
claim: ci.yml installs requirements-dev with ruff>=0.4.0 (venv has 0.17.0 which fails lint), downloads spaCy models on every run, caches ~/.cache/huggingface but the key does not include the model name, lints only mcp-server/ and tests/ (not scripts/), and runs mypy with --ignore-missing-imports.
impact_on_screened_person: A red or flaky CI lets unreviewed scoring changes land or blocks urgent corrections.
fix: Pin ruff, cache spaCy models, extend lint to scripts/, add a python-version matrix and coverage gate.

title: CI uses Python 3.14 only and test job never runs on a pinned/lock environment; no coverage or server smoke test
claim: All jobs set python-version '3.14' (no matrix, no pinned minor) with unpinned deps; the test step is plain pytest with no coverage threshold and no test that imports server.py or exercises tool_* wrappers.
impact_on_screened_person: Regressions in the MCP contract ship unnoticed.
fix: Add pytest-cov with a threshold and a tests/test_server.py wrapper contract test.

title: Golden fixtures only cover three tracked example people and encode current (possibly wrong) outputs
claim: tests/fixtures/golden_scores.json records outputs of the current algorithm as ground truth with no tolerance semantics, no EN case beyond examples, no short-text, mixed-language or adversarial fixtures. Weight changes require regenerating blindly via capture_golden.

evidence.excerpt: absence: no short-text, mixed-language, or empty-input golden cases

impact_on_screened_person: Baseline tests lock in current behaviour instead of validating it, so errors become 'expected'.
fix: Add edge-case fixtures and a documented golden-update review process.

title: Typing is weak: bare dict returns, no TypedDict/pydantic result models across tool boundaries
claim: Tool functions return dict and accept dict with string-keyed access; mypy with --ignore-missing-imports cannot catch key typos like lex['lexical_density'] vs error shape.
impact_on_screened_person: Contract drift between tools causes runtime errors that affect screened inputs.
fix: Define TypedDict/pydantic models for every tool result and enable mypy strict on tools/.

title: Config norms/edu files are loaded without schema validation; broken JSON or missing key crashes at first call
claim: _load_iq_norms/_load_edu_norms json.load with no schema/overlap/gap check (the 84.99-85 gap exists because nothing validates coverage), cached globally with no reload.
impact_on_screened_person: Bad norm edits silently misclassify people.
fix: Validate norm files against a JSON schema (contiguous bands, monotonic) at load and in a test.
